title: Query Planner and Optimizer Internals
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Query Planner and Optimizer Internals.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to parsing and analysis.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Query Planner and Optimizer Internals. Its primary job is to help you evaluate extensions, foreign-data access and internals while controlling trust, compatibility and operational scope. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing query planner and optimizer internals teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: evaluate extensions, foreign-data access and internals while controlling trust, compatibility and operational scope. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Query Planner and Optimizer Internals
content_blocks.code:
EXPLAIN (COSTS, VERBOSE)
SELECT id, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = 42;
content_blocks.expected_output: Shows the estimated plan for the SELECT without executing it. Access paths depend on schema, statistics and data distribution.
content_blocks.safety_note: Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE only when you intend to execute the statement; it runs the statement.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Assumes orders(id, total, customer_id). Compare before/after only with representative test data.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.

content_blocks.text: Version note: PostgreSQL 18.6 is the primary reference. PostgreSQL 19 beta/development features are not assumed to be stable.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Query Planner and Optimizer Internals”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Parsing and analysis”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Parsing and analysis”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Query Planner and Optimizer Internals, with an explanation of “Parsing and analysis”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Query Planner and Optimizer Internals fits into the broader goal to evaluate extensions, foreign-data access and internals while controlling trust, compatibility and operational scope.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: Parsing and analysis, Query rewriting, Planning and cost estimation.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
